A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same resilience-based offline-to-online framework and its three combinatorial applications. The complete main texts, equations, algorithms, table, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical guarantees and proofs, including in its appendices. Table 1 summarizes analytical bounds; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its new constructed counterexample is mathematical evidence, not an empirical experiment.

M1.justification: The explore-then-commit reduction retains the same per-query sampling formula, empirical averaging, and commitment to the offline algorithm's output. The same three greedy offline routines remain; renaming and revised oracle/index notation do not establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or experimental test scenarios. SC, SCSC, and FSM remain theoretical applications; additional motivational examples in v2 do not constitute new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The cited greedy algorithms are theoretically analyzed ingredients of the framework, rather than experimental comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, data splits, metrics, or evaluation budgets are reported in either version. V2's clarification of stochastic feedback concerns theoretical assumptions, not an experimental setting change.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity analyses, robustness tests, or case studies. V2's added counterexample is a formal mathematical addition assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, or significance tests. The theoretical Hoeffding concentration argument is retained, moving from v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix F.

E6.justification: Neither PDF reports measured performance, experimental rankings, or observed empirical trends. Changes to symbolic approximation guarantees and the mathematical counterexample are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix C's counterexample to a claimed noisy-oracle density bound. It changes FSM's stated approximation factor from 1−ω to 1/(1+ω) in Table 1 and Theorem 2, matching the derivation already present in v1. Appendix B also adds an explicit SC recursion base case and refines the query count to n(n+1)/2 while retaining n² as the bound used.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain the black-box conversion of resilient bi-criteria algorithms, the same T^(2/3) regret and constraint-violation rate, and resilience guarantees for SC, SCSC, and FSM. V2 foregrounds resilience more prominently, but these central contributions were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes arbitrary bounded offline perturbations from stochastic online feedback and excludes adversarial or adaptive online noise. Remark 2 newly explains why uniform resilience is preferred even though guarantees restricted to queried sets can suffice for a fixed instantiation. These add substantive applicability qualifications and rationale.

D1.justification: The sampling-budget formula and algorithm pseudocode were already supplied in v1. V2 adds no implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information; the new query-count refinement is theoretical.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning around noisy-oracle resilience. It distinguishes Wan et al.'s SCSC algorithm from Crawford et al.'s inexact-oracle analysis, adds discussion of adversarial reductions by Niazadeh et al. and Streeter and Golovin, and challenges Goyal et al.'s noisy-oracle argument. These revise substantive relationships to prior work beyond citation additions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are extensively rewritten. Offline resilience and application-specific guarantees now precede the online formulation; proofs and minimization material are redistributed across appendices. V2 also substantially expands the explanation of SC proof difficulties and adds a table of contents.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main text with a single-column journal layout, changing typography, headers, and algorithm displays. Greedy-MINTSS moves into the main text, while SCSC and FSM pseudocode move to appendices. Table 1 is restyled, and a contents page is added; no empirical plots are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the offline versus online noise assumptions, aligns the FSM approximation factor with the existing proof, and improves attribution and navigation. These provide useful accuracy and exposition gains while retaining the main method and regret guarantees. The new counterexample contains an arithmetic slip—0.98/2 is printed as 0.47—but correcting it leaves the displayed contradiction intact.
